source.title: When Trees Are Not Enough: Learning Mixed-Topology Feature Graphs with Adaptive Graph Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: Xiao-Zuo Shen; Yi-Fei Cai; Tian Tan; Rui Ning; Chun-Sheng Xin; Hong-Yi Wu

page_placements.theme: Semantic neighborhoods, feature families and hierarchy

record.tranche_reason: The study tests SAE feature-graph induction, relation validity, and causal interventions, but does not test whether sparse features are superposed as overlapping directions, whether capacity pressure explains polysemanticity, or whether SAE features are canonical or one-dimensional.
record.gate_note: The paper reports many results about mixed-topology feature graphs and SAE feature interventions. These are recorded as findings about related but different measures; they do not establish the superposition, capacity, feature-recovery, canonical-unit, or dimensionality claims in the listed versions. The paper's motivating statements and cited results about prior work are not treated as this study's results.
record.test_reason: The study trains SAEs on toy and LLM activations and reports how well its own method (AG-SAE) recovers feature-graph relations and supports interventions, compared with other SAE methods. It relies on SAE features as its unit of analysis but tests none of the versions. The toy model has 24 directions in 24 dimensions, so there are no more features than dimensions and no superposition regime, and no sparsity transition or geometry is measured (V1). Neuron polysemanticity and capacity are not studied (V2, V3). It does not test whether SAEs recover ground-truth LLM features, or whether features are spread across neurons (V4). It does not argue that SAE features are or are not canonical or stable units (V5). It does not compare 1-D with multi-dimensional features (V6). This fits T4 (method performance) more closely than T6, since SAE features are used as tools rather than merely cited.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that AG-SAE recovers reliable mixed-topology feature graphs. They also conclude it improves the dictionary (including reducing absorption) and yields stronger causal interventions than conventional SAE features. They draw no conclusions about superposition itself.
record.recipe_differences: The paper proposes and evaluates a graph-guided SAE training and refinement method, rather than reproducing the original toy-model superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported results vary across model, layer, corpus, dictionary configuration, graph relation arity, and intervention direction.

fits_no_version.finding: Mixed-topology parent relations among SAE features. In Gemma-2-2B L13 MiniPile, 23.55% of parented features are multi-parent, with multi-parent joint validity of 60.75–69.56% across settings. The toy graph is recovered exactly.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE features in LLMs are organized in multi-parent (non-tree) relations that graph-guided training can recover.

fits_no_version.finding: Leading AG-SAE features give larger addition and ablation effects than Vanilla SAE features on the first-letter task.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Structure-guided SAE training yields features with stronger single-feature causal control.

fits_no_version.finding: Conventional SAE features show substantial feature absorption: Vanilla SAE Abs. 51.39 (Table 1D), and 42.08% absorption fraction on a fixed SAE (D.5). A single realignment step reduces this to 28.11%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Feature absorption in standard SAEs is common and partly correctable by structure-guided realignment. This is related to, but not a test of, SAE features as canonical units.

record.problems: The authors state that reliable ground-truth structure is unavailable for real LLM activations. Real-model structural evidence therefore relies on activation-based diagnostics and blinded semantic judgments rather than known ground-truth relations. The reported semantic validity is below 100%, and no uncertainty estimates are provided for the Table 1 relation-validity rates.
record.rows_left_out: Many additional table entries, graph-composition counts, per-arity rates, and component-ablation measurements concern the same different construct—feature-graph learning or its optimization—and were not separately recorded. The selected rows cover the toy graph-recovery result, the principal Gemma graph and validity outcomes, the main causal intervention effects, and cross-setting joint-validity outcomes.

untested.parts: All parts. The toy model has 24 directions in 24 dimensions (no feature excess). No sparsity transition, interference or geometry is measured.
All parts. Neurons and capacity competition are not studied.
Whether LLM features are spread across neurons, and whether SAEs recover true LLM features. No ground truth exists for the LLM settings.
Completeness, stability across runs, and canonicity of SAE features are not tested. Absorption is used only as a method benchmark.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T6/'discusses' is changed to T4/'uses_without_test': SAE features are the study's working unit and the results are method performance. The absorption baseline numbers for conventional SAEs are loosely adjacent to V5 but are not framed or tested as evidence about canonicity. No verdicts are given.

versions.untested_parts: No test of excess sparse features over representational dimensions, overlapping near-orthogonal directions, sparsity-dependent superposition transitions, or regular superposition geometry. The toy model has 24 directions in 24 dimensions and evaluates parent-set recovery.
No test of neuron polysemanticity as a consequence of limited capacity or of important features receiving dedicated dimensions.
No test of polysemanticity arising without capacity pressure.
The study evaluates relations among SAE features and their interventions, not whether LLM features are spread across neurons or whether an SAE recovers ground-truth features in an LLM.
No test of whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
No comparison of one-dimensional feature directions with multi-dimensional feature representations.

relation.reason: It uses recovered SAE features as analytical units without directly testing the listed superposition versions. The toy benchmark has 24 directions in 24 dimensions; graph topology and training convergence do not establish superposition geometry or canonical representational units.

tranche.reason: The paper uses SAE feature representations to develop and evaluate graph-guided dictionary learning; its results measure its method's recovery, relation validity, absorption correction, and intervention performance.

source_check.notes: The authors-conclusion paraphrase is accurate. Retain these results as method-performance context; none supplies a direct test of the claim versions, and overall Joint must be distinguished from multi-parent validity.

Gemma-2-2B layer 13/PubMed: multi-parent Joint=60.75%. Qwen3.5-2B-Base layer 18/MiniPile: multi-parent Joint=62.25%.
statements.problem: The 23.55% topology statistic is correct, but 69.56% is overall joint validity including single-parent relations, not multi-parent joint validity.
